question_en:
The image displays a product. To confirm the product's identity and for subsequent records, please answer the following questions:

1. What are the product names and brands corresponding to Figures A, B, and C?
2. What are the years when the product was initially discontinued, made a limited-time return, and officially became a regular shelf item?
3. What are the release years for the three flavors in Figure C? Please provide the official English names for the three products shown in the figure respectively.
4. After the product became a regular shelf item, which company transferred the brand business containing it to which company? What are the dates when the buyer announced the signing of the acquisition agreement and when the seller announced the completion of the transaction?

Answer Format: Please answer in numbered points (1)–(4). Each point should only answer the corresponding part and provide all information required by that question completely.
answer:
(1) Product Name: Cheez Balls; Brand: PLANTERS.

(2) Initially discontinued: 2006; Limited-time return: 2018; Officially became a regular shelf item: 2019.

(3) All three flavors were released in 2020. Official English names: White Cheddar, Nacho, Blazin’ Hot.

(4) Transferor: The Kraft Heinz Company; Transferee: Hormel Foods Corporation; Date when the buyer announced the signing of the acquisition agreement: 2021-02-11; Date when the seller announced the completion of the transaction: 2021-06-07.

## Step 02 · Establish product candidates based on the packaging series

**Action:** Read the PLANTERS brand and Cheez Balls text in Figures A/B/C; example query: Planters Cheez Balls back flavors official.

**Evidence Observation:**

The three figures span different packaging and flavor periods and should be identified as the same product line; they must not be mistaken for Cheez Curls due to differences between old cans and new bag formats. The official 2018 return press release mentions both products simultaneously, so the Balls shown in the figure must be selected.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2018/Thanks-to-Popular-Demand-Planters-Cheez-Balls-and-Cheez-Curls-Are-Back/default.aspx
https://www.planters.com/faqs/are-cheez-balls-and-cheez-curls-still-available/

**Result of this step:** The answer to the first question is PLANTERS Cheez Balls.

## Step 03 · Verify the discontinuation year using the brand FAQ

**Action:** Read the entry "Are Cheez Balls and Cheez Curls still available".

**Evidence Observation:**

The FAQ explicitly states that Cheez Balls were discontinued in 2006 and made a limited-time return in 2018. Although subtracting the "12 years" mentioned in the news from 2018 would also yield 2006, the brand page that explicitly lists the year is more suitable for controlling the standard.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.planters.com/faqs/are-cheez-balls-and-cheez-curls-still-available/

**Result of this step:** The first time point for the second question is 2006.

## Step 04 · Verify the nature of the 2018 return

**Action:** Open the Kraft Heinz press release dated 2018-06-26 titled "Thanks to Popular Demand".

**Evidence Observation:**

The press release describes it as "limited-time," indicating that the initial return was a limited-time supply; it is not evidence of becoming an "official permanent regular shelf item." The date 2018-06-26 is the announcement date; since the final question only requires the year, report 2018.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2018/Thanks-to-Popular-Demand-Planters-Cheez-Balls-and-Cheez-Curls-Are-Back/default.aspx

**Result of this step:** The second node for the second question is the 2018 limited-time return.

## Step 05 · Check the announcement for becoming a regular shelf item

**Action:** Example query: Planters Cheez Balls are here to stay 2019; read the original press release dated 2019-08-20.

**Evidence Observation:**

The title and body text use "are here to stay" and "shelf staple," clearly indicating a transition from limited-time return to regular supply. Only after distinguishing this from the 2018 release can the official regular year 2019 be answered.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2019/Cheez-Ball-Fans-Rejoice---PLANTERS-Announces-Cheez-Balls-Are-Here-to-Stay/default.aspx

**Result of this step:** The timeline for the three periods in the second question is closed.

## Step 06 · Search for the original press release for the flavors in Figure C

**Action:** Enter the press release dated 2020-02-14 titled "For the First Time Ever" and compare the three packages in Figure C with the official names.

**Evidence Observation:**

This press release is the source for the launch of new Cheez Balls flavors, with the year 2020. The three items selected in the image must be mapped to their names one by one; other products mentioned in the entire announcement must not be listed as a fourth object in the figure.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2020/For-the-First-Time-Ever-PLANTERS-Launches-New-Cheez-Balls-Flavors-Including-Blazin-Hot/default.aspx

**Result of this step:** The common year for the third question is confirmed as 2020.

## Step 07 · Match the three English names item by item

**Action:** Copy the packaging name for each item in Figure C individually, then verify the spelling against the press release.

**Evidence Observation:**

Corresponds to White Cheddar, Nacho, and Blazin' Hot; retain the apostrophe and "Hot" in Blazin', and do not merge promotional terms or original flavor names. The three names are reported with their common release year only after being bound to their respective packages.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2020/For-the-First-Time-Ever-PLANTERS-Launches-New-Cheez-Balls-Flavors-Including-Blazin-Hot/default.aspx

**Result of this step:** The three items for the third question are completed item by item.

## Step 08 · Handle flavors in the same press release that are not in the problem figure

**Action:** Check the complete flavor list in the release against the saved source record for Figure C.

**Evidence Observation:**

The press release also involves background on a fourth flavor, but the problem figure only displays three. The question asks for the three types shown in the figure and does not require an exhaustive list of the entire series in the announcement; additional source content is used for exclusion rather than expanding the answer.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2020/For-the-First-Time-Ever-PLANTERS-Launches-New-Cheez-Balls-Flavors-Including-Blazin-Hot/default.aspx

**Result of this step:** Maintain precise wording for exactly the three types asked.

## Step 09 · Trace the transaction from the brand name

**Action:** Example query: Hormel acquisition Planters Cheez Balls February 11 2021.

**Evidence Observation:**

The buyer Hormel's official press release states the addition to the strategic brand portfolio and explicitly identifies the counterparty Kraft Heinz; the business scope includes Planters and Cheez Balls. Merely seeing the current brand ownership is insufficient to answer the transaction process; records for both the signing and the closing must be retained. The body of this transaction news retains the Planters news image entry; it is used to track articles on the same brand transaction, not as an independent basis for naming the three flavors item by item.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.hormelfoods.com/newsroom/press-releases/hormel-foods-adds-another-strategic-leading-brand-to-its-portfolio-with-the-acquisition-of-planters/
https://www.hormelfoods.com/wp-content/uploads/Newsroom_20210211_Planters.jpg

**Result of this step:** The two companies and the entry point for the signing announcement in the fourth question are located.

## Step 10 · Extract the announcement date for the signing of the agreement

**Action:** Read the Hormel press release date and the wording "definitive agreement".

**Evidence Observation:**

The date when the buyer announced the signing of the acquisition agreement is 2021-02-11; this is the signing announcement, not the closing completion date. The source domain belongs to one party to the transaction and serves as evidence for the buyer and the intended transaction scope at that time.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.hormelfoods.com/newsroom/press-releases/hormel-foods-adds-another-strategic-leading-brand-to-its-portfolio-with-the-acquisition-of-planters/

**Result of this step:** The first date is fixed as 2021-02-11.

## Step 11 · Verify the completion date from the seller's documents

**Action:** Read the official press release "Kraft Heinz Completes Sale of Nuts Business".

**Evidence Observation:**

The seller announced the completion of the transaction on 2021-06-07, with the transferee being Hormel Foods Corporation; the business list in the body includes the product in the question within the transfer. The February agreement date must not be written as the June closing date, nor should the direction of the two companies be reversed.

**Evidence Links:**

https://news.kraftheinzcompany.com/press-releases-details/2021/Kraft-Heinz-Completes-Sale-of-Nuts-Business/default.aspx

**Result of this step:** The second date for the fourth question is fixed as 2021-06-07.

## Step 12 · Review whether the chronological order is self-consistent

**Action:** Arrange the nodes in the order 2006 → 2018 → 2019 → 2020 → 2021-02-11 → 2021-06-07.

**Evidence Observation:**

Discontinuation, limited-time return, regularization, flavor expansion, and brand business transaction are each supported by official documents from the corresponding periods. The transfer of the product from Kraft Heinz to Hormel occurred after the 2019 regularization, which complies with the relational constraints in the problem statement.
